verdict: Avoid new chemical, dyes and intermediates exposure in Haldia for now; lend only to feedstock-linked, phenol/acetone-derivative borrowers with tight structure, and decline standalone dye and intermediate units.
title: Haldia Chemicals, Dyes & Intermediates: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**A chemical or dye unit here buys feedstock, runs it through reactors and sells to laminates, plywood, adhesives, resins, paints and pharma buyers.** Cash is made on conversion spread, not on volume alone, so the spread between feedstock and finished price is the whole business. **Phenol and acetone are the anchor inputs for the downstream cluster** — the new Adperma complex at Haldia carries 345,000 mt of phenol and 215,000 mt of acetone capacity [1][3]. **Capex is heavy and lumpy** — that project is a Rs 6,000-crore spend [3] — so most SMEs here are either downstream of it or competing with imported material. **Working capital sits in inventory and receivables**, and rating reports flag elevated working-capital intensity that blocks capital in high-growth phases [9].

## What has changed now
**The local demand signal is weak.** West Bengal GST collections ran -1.3% Apr-to-date against India +6.1% [D], and state electricity demand grew 5.7% against India's 9.5% [D]. **National chemical output is contracting** — IIP NIC 20 is -0.5% YoY and -1.2% Apr-to-date [D]. **The offset is supply-side:** Adperma starts commercial production by end-December 2026 [2][3], which should give downstream units domestic phenol and acetone instead of imports [1][3]. **Peer results are strong but not local** — Aarti Industries posted Q2 FY27 revenue of Rs 3,668 crore, up 75%, and PAT up 58.5% [6], on 30% volume growth [5]. Treat that as a specialty-chemistry read-across, not a Haldia signal. **Rating commentary is dated** — the CRISIL note on a 3-4% revenue recovery after a 9% dip cites Chinese dumping and de-stocking [8], and the ICRA dye-unit report is from January 2026 [11]; both are old.

## Where to grow
**Pursue borrowers that buy phenol or acetone from Adperma and sell into laminates, plywood, adhesives and resins** — they gain a freight and import-cost advantage the moment the plant runs [1][3]. **Also pursue converters with a written offtake or long-term supply agreement**, the model Aarti cites for its growth [6]. **Avoid standalone dye and intermediate units selling into fragmented textile buyers** — they carry the working-capital blockage [9] without feedstock integration. **When a proposal lands, check the feedstock source contract first; if it is spot-only, ask for the last twelve months of purchase invoices and the price-pass-through clause.**

## How to grow safely
**Structure against the conversion cycle, not the balance sheet.** Take monthly stock and receivable statements, and a monthly feedstock-versus-finished-price sheet. **If receivable days stretch beyond the stated credit period, ask for the buyer-wise ageing and stop enhancement.** **Covenant on debt-service cover and on inventory days**, and take the promoter's personal guarantee where the unit is single-product. **Collect from customer** the actual conversion margin, power tariff and contract terms — the sources do not give them.

## Early warning signs
**Watch for a downstream unit buying feedstock on spot while its own selling prices fall** — that is margin compression before it shows in GST. **Watch electricity consumption per unit of output**; a fall means idle reactors. **Watch for delayed statutory dues and salary payments**, the first visible sign of a cash squeeze in this cluster.
watch: Monthly GST returns and e-way bills (monthly)
Two consecutive months of falling outward supplies -> freeze enhancement and re-price limit
Feedstock purchase invoices vs finished sales (monthly)
Spot-only buying with falling realisations -> ask for price-pass-through clause or reduce limit
Days beyond stated credit period -> stop enhancement, seek buyer confirmation
Consumption per unit output falls -> inspect plant and confirm order book
Slippage past December 2026 -> re-assess downstream borrowers' input cost assumption
